\section[el margen]{el margen — the margin; the room}

\label{lesson:ES-C638-margen}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for advisable, then the Spanish for to suit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el margen}
\textbf{el margen} — \textquotedblleft{}the margin; the room\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No hay margen para errores.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There is no room for mistakes.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Al margen} — on the sidelines.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{margen} is inherited from Latin \emph{margo, marginis} 'edge, border', through Old Spanish \emph{margen} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el margen}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{el margen}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{el margen}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for advisable, then the Spanish for to suit, then say \emph{el margen} again
\end{itemize}

\section[limitar]{limitar — to limit}

\label{lesson:ES-C638-limitar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to suit, then the Spanish for the margin.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: limitar}
\textbf{limitar} — \textquotedblleft{}to limit\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tenemos que limitar los gastos.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We have to limit our spending.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Limitarse a} — to confine yourself to.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{limitar} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{limitare} 'to bound', built on \emph{limes} 'boundary' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[el control]{el control — the control; the check}

\label{lesson:ES-C638-control}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the margin, then the Spanish for to limit.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: el control}
\textbf{el control} — \textquotedblleft{}the control; the check\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hay un control de seguridad.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There is a security check.}
\end{quote}

\emph{El control de pasaportes} — passport control.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{control} was borrowed from French \emph{contrôle} 'a check', from Old French \emph{contrerole}, a second roll kept to check the first, from Medieval Latin \emph{contrarotulum}, built from \emph{contra} and \emph{rotulus} 'roll' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: controlar}

Regular -ar verb.

\section[excepto]{excepto — except}

\label{lesson:ES-C638-excepto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for the control, then the Spanish for to control.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: excepto}
\textbf{excepto} — \textquotedblleft{}except\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Abrimos todos los días excepto el lunes.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{We are open every day except Monday.}
\end{quote}

Means the same as \emph{salvo} and \emph{menos}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{excepto} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{exceptus} 'taken out', the participle of \emph{excipere}, from \emph{capere} 'to take' (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{excepto}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for the control, then the Spanish for to control, then say \emph{excepto} again
\end{itemize}
